title.narrative: UNESCO/Keizo Obuchi Research Fellowships Programme, Phase VIII - 2025/2026 Cycle

description.narrative:
UNESCO/Japan Young Researchers’ Fellowship Programme (UNESCO/Keizo Obuchi Research Fellowships Programme) aims to enrich and strengthen capacity of the stakeholders in the areas of the scientific knowledge in the fields of Heritage conservation and management, Sustainable Development (including Education for sustainable development) as well as Artificial Intelligence (AI). Specifically, the project seeks to achieve the following outcome:
The young researchers meaningfully undertake research in the fields of Heritage conservation and management, Sustainable Development (including Education for sustainable development) and Artificial Intelligence (AI) and engage in the sharing and transfer of knowledge with National Commissions, universities and institutions through the fellowship in Japan.
This outcome will be realized through the delivery of 2 outputs, encompassing 3 key activities hereunder:
Output N°1: Capacities of the young researchers strengthened by following the courses in the universities and other institutions in the fields of Heritage conservation and management, Sustainable Development (including Education for Sustainable Development) and Artificial Intelligence.
1. Select 20 fellows (10 for each of the 2 cycles) and coordinate the placement of these fellows to conduct their research at the Japanese Universities.
Output N°2: The young researchers enabled to meaningfully engage at national, sub-regional and regional levels, and share their knowledge and expertise with National Commissions as well as universities and institutions specialized in the fields of Heritage conservation and management, Sustainable Development (including Education for sustainable development) and Artificial Intelligence (AI).
1. Increase visibility and awareness of National Commissions and stakeholders at national, sub-regional and regional levels on the proceedings and results of fellowships programme. 2. Communicate the research conducted by the fellows through various channels include webpage and the communication tools of National Commissions.
